quest.title: Underground Crime
quest.description: A new clue discovered in Rawat's mother's residence seems to be a critical piece of evidence allowing the investigation to proceed.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's Officer Morgane, they're already here!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: We came as soon as we heard the news... I can't believe we were so careless. The most crucial information of all was hiding right there, in that room, and we missed it...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Don't blame yourself. Right now, we need to focus on finding a way in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a mechanical door over here... Hopefully the instructions in Rawat's journal will help us open it.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: It's open. Let's go in.

dialogues.speaker: "Odilon"
dialogues.text: The Marechaussee Phantom? How did they find this place!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... it's that guard from the Fortress...

dialogues.speaker: "Odilon"
dialogues.text: That's right, I'm on your side! Uh... I mean, the Duke sent me. What's the matter? Some sort of mixup?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Mr. Odilon, didn't I tell you a few days ago that you need to stop all field work until you've recovered?

dialogues.speaker: "Odilon"
dialogues.text: Ah, well, y'know... Gotta help His Grace out, share the load! *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Officer Morgane, this man is an impostor. The real Mr. Odilon has no recent health issues.

dialogues.speaker: "Odilon"
dialogues.text: What? But, I...

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Looks like the Head Nurse was right about the face-swapping method... Arrest them all!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Dupont, stay here and keep guard — and watch the exit. If we're not back soon, call for reinforcements.

dialogues.speaker: Dupont
dialogues.text: Got it!

dialogues.speaker: Dupont
dialogues.text: Captain! According to our list, many of the fugitives aren't accounted for. There may be others hiding deeper inside the facility.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Ah. So these guys were just the lookout crew...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So many jars. Was this some sort of production facility?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: This scent... It's probably the ingredients used to make Butterfly Dew.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How come they're all empty? Did it sell so well that he ran out of supplies?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: How strange... Why would Rawat choose to manufacture a popular product like that in such a difficult-to-reach location?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Given our suspicion that he may have been coerced into the illegal drug trade, I would have thought that any production facility we find here would be used for illicit purposes.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Perhaps Butterfly Dew is itself an illegal drug.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Do you have any evidence for that claim?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: No, just a guess. We need to find Rawat as soon as possible. He has all the answers we need.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Understood. Well, let's not linger here. Let's go, come on!

talks.objective: Look for a way to go deeper

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This room's much smaller than the others.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Judging by the implements on the table, this looks like a potion-making lab.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Head Nurse! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... Huh, Rawat's clothes? Why would he change here?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hmm... Perhaps they stripped him down, left the clothes behind, and disposed of him somewhere else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes, Sigewinne, where did that come from!?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: What a tragic way to go... Especially with such a bright future ahead of him...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: There's a path leading further on, Officer Morgane. Let's keep up the pace.

talks.objective: Head into the deepest part of the lab

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Shh! There's a whole bunch of people in there!

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: Are you serious? You're telling us that within a day, our faces are going to rot like yours?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Fontainian physiology changed dramatically after that great flood, and it's not as compatible with this face-changing solution as before. The side effects are as you can see.

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: Why didn't you say anything before we all used it!?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Look. My plan got you all out of prison, didn't it? You'd have much bigger problems to worry about right now if the Marechaussee Phantom found out about your other crimes... Consider an ugly mug getting off lightly.

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: Ugh, you're just lucky we didn't leave you in there, after you disappeared on us with no warning! We only let it slide 'cause we're former partners... and now you have the gall to pull a stunt like this?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: "Partners"? Make no mistake, each of us is only looking out for himself. If you place too much trust in others, well I'm afraid that's your problem.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: You hid things from me, too. Remember how you each had a spare potion, yet kept quiet about it until we planned the prison break?

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: Oh, and you didn't have a secret spare? Then do you wanna explain how you melted your face off before all this?

dialogues.speaker: "Erick"
dialogues.text: Guys, that's enough, calm down. It is what it is. Arguing won't change anything.

dialogues.speaker: "Erick"
dialogues.text: What's the plan, Potton? I'm assuming you brought us here for a reason?

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: There is no plan! We followed him here on the promise of more juice, but it turns out there ain't a drop here!

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: Besides, what does it matter now anyway? He already said, even if we did get our hands on more of that stuff, switching faces again solves nothing. They're still gonna melt off eventually.

dialogues.speaker: "Erick"
dialogues.text: I said, enough arguing! Potton, tell us the plan.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Hmph. The most practical solution is to continue using the potion. Keep switching to a new face before the ulcers can start forming.

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: Are you kidding me? This stuff was hard enough to get hold of even when we had a supply. Now you're asking us to use it like skin lotion, after the flood all but wiped the supply out!?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Well, there is another option. But you'll have to make a deal with me first.

dialogues.speaker: "Erick"
dialogues.text: Okay, now we're talking. What's the deal?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: I have a document I took from that researcher that details how to make a replacement. Just give me one bottle of the undiluted fluid, and I will get to work.

dialogues.speaker: "Erick"
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: What's the problem? I thought you always kept reserves? Or did you really just have one spare bottle each?

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: What do you think? That we were shipping them into the Fortress of Meropide by the basketload?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Well then... say hello to never showing your marred faces in public again!

dialogues.speaker: "Houilles"
dialogues.text: Gah, I've heard enough! Get him! Let's see if that document even exists!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Freeze! Marechaussee Phantom!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: What? Who let them in?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Officer Morgane, before anything else, please find out Rawat's status.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Rawat...

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: I don't see him... Hand over the hostage now, if you want any chance of avoiding an extension to your sentences.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Spare us your condescending attempts to coax us back to our cells! You think we're looking to negotiate? Rawat is dead!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Potton...

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Arrest them all! Don't let anyone get away!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Gotta say, I never expected to see the head nurse in combat...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Some patients respond better to a more aggressive treatment plan. Did we get everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Dupond
dialogues.text: Captain, we've finished the headcount — Potton's missing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Over there! The door's closing!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Hah, one group trying to arrest me, another trying to hunt me down... Good, I get to kill two birds with one stone.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: How did he get up there? There must be a secret passage somewhere. Find it!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Don't waste your energy. I already sealed it off.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: How naive. We have more people outside. If we're not back out by the agreed time, they'll come to our rescue.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Well then, you'd better hope they get here in time!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: There's some kind of gas leaking from the pipes... Be careful, it's poisonous.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: This is our distribution center, where we store the product derived from our source solution. We had to use special fire prevention methods to prevent contamination.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: The pipe network here was designed to emit a gas for firefighting. One little modification later, and it makes an efficient death trap.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Why would you do this? Your partners are here too.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Oh, please. If they can't supply what I need, they're of no further use to me. Besides, I can't have them exposing my potential whereabouts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's a maniac... C'mon, we've gotta find a way to open that door!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Go ahead, struggle in vain. Once the last of you croaks, no one will ever find me again. So long!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Are you sure you're ready to leave, Potton? You haven't changed your dressing today.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: ...You can't cure my face. Just give up.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: And what if I could?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Hmph... Nice try, you're just trying to stall me. Don't you worry about me, I'll find a way to cure my face once I get out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Oh, I doubt it. After all, Fontainians can no longer dissolve in Primordial Seawater.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: What the... How did you...!?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: The key component of the face-changing potion is the fluid left behind by dissolved Fontainians. It might look like ordinary water, but it has some unique elements in it.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Before the flood, all Fontainians were Oceanids, physiologically speaking.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: A potion made from that fluid could dissolve and reconstruct the face of a Fontainian, in much the same way as Hydro Eidolons change form.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Theoretically, it could give someone any appearance they wished.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: But since the flood, Fontainians have become true humans. They can no longer provide the source material for this potion, nor reap its benefits.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Are you saying... this potion is made from Fontainians dissolved with Primordial Seawater? Then their crimes are far worse than I thought...

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: How could you know all of this? No, wait... Hahaha, of course! Well, well. So that's why you have a human appearance.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: It also means that I have a formula you're unaware of. *cough* ...The air's getting thicker... It's getting hard to breathe.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Heh, I might get to make a deal today after all. Alright, keep talking. How do you intend to give me the formula?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Oh, it's not a formula, but a finished product. I have a bottle of it right here.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: When I tried Rawat's skincare product, I noticed it had a certain special component in it. So I had my friends gather some other ingredients for me, and sure enough, a little experimenting later, I'd produced the potion.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'm guessing his skincare lotion contains the fruits of your joint research?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Huh. Impressive guesswork. Yeah, we were his supplier for some of the raw ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *gasp*

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: But it only contains a tiny amount of the active ingredient. The effect is miniscule compared to the undiluted fluid.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Well, I found a way to reverse the dilution process, giving the skincare lotion a similar effect to the fluid it is derived from.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: That's impossible...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: If I tell you some of the ingredients, I think you can figure it out. First, you need to combine Tainted Hydro Phantasm tissue with Transoceanic Pearls at a ratio of around three to seven.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Tainted Hydro Phantasms and Transoceanic Pearls? Ah, I see... Can't believe I never thought of that...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: So. Can we make a deal?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Sounds good to me. There's a delivery pipeline beneath this window. Drop the potion in, and I'll release you all.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Nope, not trusting you that easily. You're like those naughty kids who try to hide their illness. Open the sluice gate first, then I'll hand you the potion.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Hmph. Even if you're not bluffing, your potion won't cure my face permanently... You really think you have any leverage here?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: I'm not closing the valve this time. Clock's ticking.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Fine, then I'll just stand here with the potion in my hand. And when I faint from the poison, I'll drop it and it'll be destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: No...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's open!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Disable that sluice gate! Jam it! Don't let it close again!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: That's more like it. In that case, a promise is a promise.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Head Nurse, there's too much poison gas in here. We have to leave, now!

talks.objective: Get out via the way you came

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... That was too close! That Potton is a real nasty piece of work...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Don't be too quick to sit down. Moving around a little will help relieve the soreness.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #Same goes for you, {NICKNAME}. But Paimon, you should be fine, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Flying fast is pretty tiring too, actually! Anyway, that's not important right now. Paimon's still shocked to learn that there was a whole criminal operation going on behind that skincare lotion.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Shame I ended up giving the improved version to Potton after finally making it for you... I'll make you some more, I promise.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No no no, please don't... Paimon doesn't wanna use that stuff anymore. Still, it was a pretty good job that Paimon wanted to buy some in the first place, huh? It ended up saving everyone's lives! That's gotta count for something.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sigewinne was the one doing the saving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah, Paimon was just kidding...

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Head Nurse, I've done a final headcount of our team and the criminals. Everyone's here and doing fine. We're ready to escort the fugitives back to the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: It's a shame that we didn't find Rawat. At this point, I'm afraid he's probably deceased.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* What a horrible bunch. Especially that Potton guy. If he hadn't made good on that deal, we'd all be dead because of him.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: No we wouldn't. I always keep a whole of bunch antidotes on me for emergencies, and one of them neutralizes that poison gas. We'd have been fine, even if he hadn't opened the gate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Then why did you give him the potion?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: ...If this is true, I must concur. Sorry to be blunt, but I think you made a bad decision by handing him that bottle.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: If he changes his appearance and flees Fontaine, it's unlikely that we'll ever find him, no matter how cooperative his accomplices are when we question them.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: No, you don't understand. I gave him the potion precisely so we could be sure where he'll go next.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: We gotta hurry. She won't last much longer.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Don't move a muscle! I might be short, but I pack a mean punch!

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: Captain? You're just in time. While I was lying in wait, I spotted this crook snooping around, trying to find a way in. So I detained him.

dialogues.speaker: Intruder
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, his face...

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Are you... Potton? So this is where you were heading, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: This is how Potton looked before his face was marred. His current appearance matches the mugshot on his arrest warrant.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hmm... I see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so what's going on? Wasn't the whole point of the potion to disguise himself and escape Fontaine? Why would change back to his original face and run right into our trap!?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Enough of this nonsense! Let me in!

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: You better pipe down! There's an old lady in there who's very sick. No way are we letting a crook like you inside!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Ugh, to heck with it... Listen to me! I'm Rawat! That's my mother in there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's gotta be lying, right? Rawat was a victim in all this, he was forced into it against his will... How could he and this monster be the same person?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Forced against his will? Hahahaha... That's the funniest thing I've heard all day.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Back when I was being coerced, everyone thought I was colluding of my own free will. And then when I actually became a criminal in my own right, you all suddenly thought I must be under duress!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Amazing what a difference a handsome face makes!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Save us the speech. Explain yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: You want an explanation? Fine, I'll tell it how it is.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: When I was just Potton, the whole world treated me with contempt.

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: Ew. What do you want? Get away from me...

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Women despised me.

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: Collaborate? Pff, you don't look like much of a researcher to me...

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: My peers scorned me.

dialogues.speaker: Enri
dialogues.text: Mr. Potton, was it? I'm most interested in your research. Consider my offer carefully — I doubt you'll find other investment opportunities.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Only villains would work with me.

dialogues.speaker: Gascon
dialogues.text: You want out of the game? Forget about it. Turns out I slipped up a little — left your picture with some Marechaussee Phantom officers... Easy mistake to make. Now they've listed you as an accomplice and drawn up an arrest warrant.

dialogues.speaker: Gascon
dialogues.text: So I suggest you put any thoughts of running away to rest.... If you get caught by the Gardes for being in the Sinthe business, you ain't ever seeing the light of day again! Hahahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: There was no way out for me...

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Until... I could stop being Potton.

dialogues.speaker: Audree
dialogues.text: Mr. Rawat, I, um... I have something I'd like to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: I became popular with women.

dialogues.speaker: Antibes
dialogues.text: This new potion you've developed is fascinating — genius, in fact! Would you consider working with me? I'd be happy to sign a licensing agreement...

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: My peers looked up to me.

dialogues.speaker: Enri
dialogues.text: I'm very interested in your research, Sir. You must no doubt have offers from countless investors, so far be it from me to ask for a full collaboration, per se — I merely wanted to express my interest... No pressure at all, naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: And the villains even began to fear me.

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: Becoming Rawat showed me what a superficial world we live in.

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: But I did not hold a grudge. After all, this superficiality could be made to work in my favor.

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: Or so I thought... But alas, the world seemed bent on finding a reason to make me despise it.

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: Mother, I'm back! How are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: ...Hmm... Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: I bought the best medicine Mora could buy, but nothing would cure her illness... In the end, I hoped at least that she could see her son one last time before she passed, but...

dialogues.speaker: Rawat
dialogues.text: ...When everyone else rejected me, the only person who cared about me was my mother. Then, when I became a rising star in the Fontaine Research Institute, I was unrecognizable to her.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: I have to let her see me again, even if it means donning my own wretched, ugly face...

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: ...Well? Is that enough explaining for you? Now do you understand? Let me inside already!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Have you ever considered if you'll even be able to look your mother in the eyes, after what you've done?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: You found a way to completely change your identity. You could easily have escaped from them... But no, you chose to keep working with them!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Hmph, why would I want to give up on such a lucrative business? The profits were dozens of times that of the Sinthe business, and it was all above board!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you kept being a villain just for the money!

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Villain? By what standard? Is doing evil deeds really what makes someone a villain in your eyes, or does it all come down to the way they look? None of you saw a villain when I was wearing my other face, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: You have no right to judge me! You're all just fake people living in a hypocritical world. I regret nothing! My mother would understand!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... You're a villain to the core! But especially that tongue!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Honestly, I don't see a villain when I look at your current face, either.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Don't humor me. You don't seem surprised by my confession in the least. How long have you known the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I didn't know anything for sure until you chose to take that potion bottle and spare our lives. But if you're asking when I started suspecting you, it was the first time you came to see me at the infirmary.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I had to confirm my suspicions. That's why I chose to join this investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Are you kidding me? A young, promising researcher and a wretched criminal? What on earth gave you the idea that they could be one and the same person?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Well, there were no visual clues — this potion's face-changing effects are very powerful. Even as a Melusine, I couldn't see through the disguise.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: But I believe I understand humanity a little better than most of my kind. Humans have certain fundamental qualities that do not change with their appearance.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Fundamental qualities, huh? So, you think you're the one who's seen through me, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Most people probably don't know this, but I think I can guess what your deal is. Melusine constitutions are very close to that of water, so it stands to reason that the potion should work on them, too.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: You used it yourself, didn't you? That's why you have a human appearance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sigewinne?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Yes, you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Haha... I'll bet it was back in the days when Melusines were discriminated against because of their appearance.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: It was either carry on living in the gutters as part of an alien race cast out by humanity, or become the Head Nurse of the Fortress of Meropide, revered by all. Not a hard choice to make. It's a no-brainer.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: So you see? You and I, we're the same! And I'm the one who saw through you!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: That's not important right now. You came here to see your mother, didn't you? Well, I can grant you your wish.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Head Nurse, I'm not sure that's a good idea in his current state.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Don't worry. Back in the warehouse when I traded the potion for our lives, I was doing it to test him.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: He was willing to risk sacrificing his only chance of escaping capture by opening the gate in exchange for the potion, all so he could see his mother again. If nothing else, his concern for his mother is genuine.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #So before you arrest him, please allow him to see his mother one last time. {NICKNAME} and I will accompany him — you have nothing to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Alright. I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Mom? It's me, Potton, your son! You recognize me now... don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Mom...! What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but I have some bad news. I examined your mother last time we were here, and it appears that due to her prolonged fever, she's... lost her eyesight.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Your appearance no longer has any bearing on her ability to recognize you. But... there are always other ways to remind our loved ones who we are... wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: No no, it can't be... Please, Mom, open your eyes! It's me, your son, Potton! If... If you really can't see my face, then... here, take my hand... Tell me you feel your son's hand!

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: I've done so much to get to this point... Please, you have to recognize me...

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: No, no, no... No!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hm, the temperature of his palm must have changed. ...I'm sorry. It seems I couldn't bring him back to you after all.

dialogues.speaker: Sick Old Lady
dialogues.text: ...Ahh, it's you... Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Oh... Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Mom... Why will you answer her, and not me? Why? Why!?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: No more questions, Potton. She's gone.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Mom! Mom...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'm sorry to say this, Potton, but you and I are not the same.

dialogues.speaker: Potton
dialogues.text: Hmph... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Potton is eventually taken away by members of the Marechaussee Phantom. A day passes in a flash.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: No, don't look this way. I'm supposed to be hiding, remember? Captain's orders.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Join the Head Nurse inside. If he tries anything, anything at all, shout.

dialogues.speaker: Ceasth
dialogues.text: I don't trust this guy much. Be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Dupont
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I got this covered.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Potton is eventually taken away by members of the Marechaussee Phantom. A day passes in a flash.

dialogues.speaker: Lazare
dialogues.text: How did they get in here?

dialogues.speaker: Dupont
dialogues.text: Captain, up ahead! Those look like our fugitives!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: So they found this place too... Don't let any of them escape!
